name: The two elders who accused Susanna
charge: Attempted adultery by extortion; false witness against an innocent woman
summary: Two ancients of the people were appointed judges that year, of whom the Lord had said that wickedness came from Babylon from ancient judges who seemed to govern the people (Susanna 1:5). They saw Susanna walking daily in her husband’s garden, perverted their own mind, and turned away their eyes so as not to look toward heaven nor remember just judgments (Susanna 1:6-9). They hid themselves, demanded that she lie with them, and when she refused they swore before the assembly that they had taken her with a young man (Susanna 1:19-21; Susanna 1:36-41). Daniel examined them apart, their answers did not agree, and the assembly did to them what they had intended for her.
offenseFull: The record marks them as judges before adulterers, and the teaching sets the case among leaders bound in their own sin: Eli’s sons, who lay with the women at the door of the tabernacle and made the Lord’s people to transgress (1 Samuel 2:22-25), and the man who says a man should not commit adultery and commits it, through whom the name of God is blasphemed (Romans 2:21-24). These two kept much at Joacim’s house, where every suit at law came, and used the standing it gave them (Susanna 1:6). Their lust was inflamed by watching her, and the teaching traces the order of it: coveting comes first and is already adultery in the heart, and the watching day after day carries a man from the thought to the act (Matthew 5:27-28; Susanna 1:7-12). They were ashamed to declare it even to each other until they were caught in the same place, and then appointed a time together (Susanna 1:10-14). A man who goes on until he is bound with his sins is past the reach of a scripture (2 Esdras 16:77).

They hid in the garden, and when she sent the maids away they rose up and ran to her, saying that nobody could see them, and that if she would not consent they would bear witness that a young man had been with her (Susanna 1:15-21). When she cried out, they cried out against her, and one of them opened the garden door so that the servants would come in on their account of it (Susanna 1:24-27). The next day they came to the assembly full of mischievous imagination to put her to death, and commanded that her face be uncovered, that they might be filled with her beauty even while they were killing her (Susanna 1:28-32). Then they laid their hands upon her head and testified that a young man had come to her and been too strong for them to hold, and the assembly believed them as the elders and judges of the people and condemned her to death (Susanna 1:34-41). It is what the law forbids in one line, not to raise a false report nor put the hand with the wicked (Exodus 23:1).
judgmentFull: The Lord heard her voice and raised up the spirit of a young youth named Daniel, who cried that he was clear from the blood of this woman and rebuked the assembly for condemning a daughter of Israel without examination, and he had the two put apart, one far from another (Susanna 1:44-52). To the first he said that he was waxen old in wickedness, that the sins he had committed before were come to

light, and that he had pronounced false judgment, condemning the innocent and letting the guilty go free; then he asked under what tree he had seen them, got a mastick tree, and told him he had lied against his own head and that the angel of God had the sentence to cut him in two (Susanna 1:52-55). To the second he said that beauty had deceived him and lust had perverted his heart, that this was how the two had dealt with the daughters of Israel, who for fear kept company with them, but that the daughter of Juda would not abide their wickedness; he asked the same question, got a holm tree, and gave the same answer (Susanna 1:56-59). The teaching notes the name Daniel uses for him, seed of Chanaan and not of Juda, read the way Ezekiel reads it, that a man of the nation who goes on in this becomes another nation in his conduct (Ezekiel 16:3).

The whole assembly praised God that saves them that trust in him and rose up against the two elders, because Daniel had convicted them of false witness by their own mouth; then, according to the law of Moses, they did to them as they had maliciously intended to do to their neighbour and put them to death, and innocent blood was saved that day (Susanna 1:60-62). That is the statute exactly: when a witness testifies falsely against his brother, what he thought to have done to his brother is done to him, and the evil is put away (Deuteronomy 19:16-19). The teaching closes on what a lying tongue can do, that a backbiting tongue has disquieted many, pulled down strong cities and cast out virtuous women (Ecclesiasticus 28:14-15), and on the company such a charge puts a man in, since false witnesses rose against David, against Christ, and against the apostles (Psalms 27:12; Psalms 35:11; Matthew 26:59-60; Acts 6:13). It adds one warning to everyone else in the room: the man who sees an unrighteous judgment and stays quiet will answer for it with the one who began it (Proverbs 24:10-12).

lawsResolved.text: You shall not bear false witness against another nor raise a false report.
A false witness is to be punished.
If someone gives contrary testimony, then the judges shall make diligent inquisition between both men to see if the witness is a false witness.
If a witness is found to be a false witness by testifying falsely against his brother, then he shall receive the punishment that the accused brethren would have received if guilty.
The judge that justifies the wicked and condemns the just is an abomination to God.
Do not to lust after the beauty of women.
The adulterer and adulteress are to be put to death.

text.text: The same year were appointed two of the ancients of the people to be judges, such as the Lord spake of, that wickedness came from Babylon from ancient judges, who seemed to govern the people.
These kept much at Joacim’s house: and all that had any suits in law came unto them.
Now when the people departed away at noon, Susanna went into her husband’s garden to walk.
And the two elders saw her going in every day, and walking; so that their lust was inflamed toward her.
And they perverted their own mind, and turned away their eyes, that they might not look unto heaven, nor remember just judgments.
Now Eli was very old, and heard all that his sons did unto all Israel; and how they lay with the women that assembled at the door of the tabernacle of the congregation.
And he said unto them, Why do ye such things? for I hear of your evil dealings by all this people.
Nay, my sons; for it is no good report that I hear: ye make the Lord’s people to transgress.

If one man sin against another, the judge shall judge him: but if a man sin against the Lord, who shall intreat for him? Notwithstanding they hearkened not unto the voice of their father, because the Lord would slay them.
Thou therefore which teachest another, teachest thou not thyself? thou that preachest a man should not steal, dost thou steal?
Thou that sayest a man should not commit adultery, dost thou commit adultery? thou that abhorrest idols, dost thou commit sacrilege?
Thou that makest thy boast of the law, through breaking the law dishonourest thou God?
For the name of God is blasphemed among the Gentiles through you, as it is written.
Ye have heard that it was said by them of old time, Thou shalt not commit adultery:
But I say unto you, That whosoever looketh on a woman to lust after her hath committed adultery with her already in his heart.
And albeit they both were wounded with her love, yet durst not one shew another his grief.
For they were ashamed to declare their lust, that they desired to have to do with her.
Yet they watched diligently from day to day to see her.
And the one said to the other, Let us now go home: for it is dinner time.

So when they were gone out, they parted the one from the other, and turning back again they came to the same place; and after that they had asked one another the cause, they acknowledged their lust: then appointed they a time both together, when they might find her alone.

Woe be unto them that are bound with their sins, and covered with their iniquities like as a field is covered over with bushes, and the path thereof covered with thorns, that no man may travel through!
And it fell out, as they watched a fit time, she went in as before with two maids only, and she was desirous to wash herself in the garden: for it was hot.
And there was no body there save the two elders, that had hid themselves, and watched her.
Then she said to her maids, Bring me oil and washing balls, and shut the garden doors, that I may wash me.
And they did as she bade them, and shut the garden doors, and went out themselves at privy doors to fetch the things that she had commanded them: but they saw not the elders, because they were hid.
Now when the maids were gone forth, the two elders rose up, and ran unto her, saying,
Behold, the garden doors are shut, that no man can see us, and we are in love with thee; therefore consent unto us, and lie with us.
If thou wilt not, we will bear witness against thee, that a young man was with thee: and therefore thou didst send away thy maids from thee.
With that Susanna cried with a loud voice: and the two elders cried out against her.
Then ran the one, and opened the garden door.
So when the servants of the house heard the cry in the garden, they rushed in at the privy door, to see what was done unto her.
But when the elders had declared their matter, the servants were greatly ashamed: for there was never such a report made of Susanna.
And it came to pass the next day, when the people were assembled to her husband Joacim, the two elders came also full of mischievous imagination against Susanna to put her to death;
And said before the people, Send for Susanna, the daughter of Chelcias, Joacim’s wife. And so they sent.
So she came with her father and mother, her children, and all her kindred.
Now Susanna was a very delicate woman, and beauteous to behold.
And these wicked men commanded to uncover her face, (for she was covered) that they might be filled with her beauty.
Then the two elders stood up in the midst of the people, and laid their hands upon her head.
And she weeping looked up toward heaven: for her heart trusted in the Lord.
And the elders said, As we walked in the garden alone, this woman came in with two maids, and shut the garden doors, and sent the maids away.
Then a young man, who there was hid, came unto her, and lay with her.
Then we that stood in a corner of the garden, seeing this wickedness, ran unto them.
And when we saw them together, the man we could not hold: for he was stronger than we, and opened the door, and leaped out.
But having taken this woman, we asked who the young man was, but she would not tell us: these things do we testify.
Then the assembly believed them as those that were the elders and judges of the people: so they condemned her to death.
Thou shalt not raise a false report: put not thine hand with the wicked to be an unrighteous witness.
And the Lord heard her voice.
Therefore when she was led to be put to death, the Lord raised up the holy spirit of a young youth whose name was Daniel:
Who cried with a loud voice, I am clear from the blood of this woman.
Then all the people turned them toward him, and said, What mean these words that thou hast spoken?
So he standing in the midst of them said, Are ye such fools, ye sons of Israel, that without examination or knowledge of the truth ye have condemned a daughter of Israel?
Return again to the place of judgment: for they have borne false witness against her.
Then said Daniel unto them, Put these two aside one far from another, and I will examine them.
So when they were put asunder one from another, he called one of them, and said unto him, O thou that art waxen old in wickedness, now thy sins which thou hast committed aforetime are come to light.
For thou hast pronounced false judgment and hast condemned the innocent and hast let the guilty go free; albeit the Lord saith, The innocent and righteous shalt thou not slay.
Now then, if thou hast seen her, tell me, Under what tree sawest thou them companying together? Who answered, Under a mastick tree.
And Daniel said, Very well; thou hast lied against thine own head; for even now the angel of God hath received the sentence of God to cut thee in two.
So he put him aside, and commanded to bring the other, and said unto him, O thou seed of Chanaan, and not of Juda, beauty hath deceived thee, and lust hath perverted thine heart.
Thus have ye dealt with the daughters of Israel, and they for fear companied with you: but the daughter of Juda would not abide your wickedness.
Now therefore tell me, Under what tree didst thou take them companying together? Who answered, Under an holm tree.
Then said Daniel unto him, Well; thou hast also lied against thine own head: for the angel of God waiteth with the sword to cut thee in two, that he may destroy you.
And say, Thus saith the Lord God unto Jerusalem; Thy birth and thy nativity is of the land of Canaan; thy father was an Amorite, and thy mother an Hittite.
With that all the assembly cried out with a loud voice, and praised God, who saveth them that trust in him.
And they arose against the two elders, for Daniel had convicted them of false witness by their own mouth:
And according to the law of Moses they did unto them in such sort as they maliciously intended to do to their neighbour: and they put them to death. Thus the innocent blood was saved the same day.
If a false witness rise up against any man to testify against him that which is wrong;
Then both the men, between whom the controversy is, shall stand before the Lord, before the priests and the judges, which shall be in those days;
And the judges shall make diligent inquisition: and, behold, if the witness be a false witness, and hath testified falsely against his brother;
Then shall ye do unto him, as he had thought to have done unto his brother: so shalt thou put the evil away from among you.
A backbiting tongue hath disquieted many, and driven them from nation to nation: strong cities hath it pulled down, and overthrown the houses of great men.
A backbiting tongue hath cast out virtuous women, and deprived them of their labours.
Deliver me not over unto the will of mine enemies: for false witnesses are risen up against me, and such as breathe out cruelty.
False witnesses did rise up; they laid to my charge things that I knew not.
Now the chief priests, and elders, and all the council, sought false witness against Jesus, to put him to death;
But found none: yea, though many false witnesses came, yet found they none. At the last came two false witnesses,
And set up false witnesses, which said, This man ceaseth not to speak blasphemous words against this holy place, and the law:
If thou faint in the day of adversity, thy strength is small.
If thou forbear to deliver them that are drawn unto death, and those that are ready to be slain;

If thou sayest, Behold, we knew it not; doth not he that pondereth the heart consider it? and he that keepeth thy soul, doth not he know it? and shall not he render to every man according to his works?
Now when the maids were gone forth, the two elders rose up, and ran unto her, saying,
Behold, the garden doors are shut, that no man can see us, and we are in love with thee; therefore consent unto us, and lie with us.
If thou wilt not, we will bear witness against thee, that a young man was with thee: and therefore thou didst send away thy maids from thee.
Then Susanna sighed, and said, I am straitened on every side: for if I do this thing, it is death unto me: and if I do it not I cannot escape your hands.
It is better for me to fall into your hands, and not do it, than to sin in the sight of the Lord.
With that Susanna cried with a loud voice: and the two elders cried out against her.
Then ran the one, and opened the garden door.
So when the servants of the house heard the cry in the garden, they rushed in at the privy door, to see what was done unto her.
But when the elders had declared their matter, the servants were greatly ashamed: for there was never such a report made of Susanna.

So he standing in the midst of them said, Are ye such fools, ye sons of Israel, that without examination or knowledge of the truth ye have condemned a daughter of Israel?
